source_verification.basis: Published full text has matching authors/DOI, Indian state-level ASI microdata description and a negative-binomial regression on pharmaceutical firm starts. A coauthor’s public research profile independently lists the same paper. The study explicitly constructs its historical sample from units surviving by 2018–19, so attrition means its counts do not reconstruct every firm ever started. Its regressions demonstrate associations rather than causal effects; no contemporary 2026 projections follow. Caution: Historical survivor bias; independent replication and journal peer-review rigor not demonstrated. No ability to generalize to failed firms or current start-up formation rates.

aboutness.basis: Paper’s verified firm-level study explicitly analyzes Indian pharmaceutical start-up patterns across Indian states using historical Annual Survey of Industries records.
aboutness.verified_excerpt: Negative-binomial regressions of Indian-state pharmaceutical firm entry among units observed surviving up to the historical ASI window.

topic.label: Start-ups
topic.basis: Drivers of pharmaceutical start-up formation are the explicit outcome.

futures.mechanism: Historical Indian regional innovation/agglomeration and infrastructure factors associated with pharmaceutical industrial entry, subject to survival/selection.
futures.why_could_matter: If the observed regional correlations survive independent tests with complete entry/exit data, the patterns could help prioritize research on innovation clusters and pharmaceutical entrepreneurship.
futures.uncertainty: Historical survivor bias; independent replication and journal peer-review rigor not demonstrated. No ability to generalize to failed firms or current start-up formation rates.
futures.research_question: Do the regional correlations persist when failed firms and actual entry/exit histories are included in India’s pharmaceutical start-up data?

second_pass_audit.finding: Full 2025 journal PDF directly confirms a historically grounded Indian-state count-data analysis with negative binomial regression on pharmaceutical firm formation, using Annual Survey of Industries records dating 1981–2018. It is not a study of 2025–2026 startup registrations. Journal claims peer review but no external methodological replication or independently established editorial review was located; the journal website itself inconsistently describes quarterly publication and two issues per year.
second_pass_audit.remaining_limitations: Specific historical correlations are the maximum supported inference; startup-causation and contemporary India forecasts are unwarranted. Publisher’s own claims about peer review are not independent corroboration.
second_pass_audit.required_for_next_upgrade_or_reconsidera: Reproduce regressions from Annual Survey of Industries data and compare with post-2018 Ministry of Corporate Affairs/Startup India records.
